items.title: DocXEval: A Systematic Evaluation of Explainability in Multimodal Document Understanding
items.summary_1line: Multimodal transformer models have driven unprecedented performance breakthroughs in modern document understanding. However, the inherent black-box nature of these models remains a major obstacle to their safe deploym...
items.editor_note: Shifts focus from accuracy to explainability evaluation of multimodal document understanding.

editorial.tldr: An Oct 9 arXiv paper split multimodal document QA agents into role-specialized locate, judge and read tools over a knowledge-point index. Until Oct 27, no follow-up appeared in the feed.
editorial.whats_new: Two Oct 27 papers extend the thread: RouteDRAG learns to route and control agentic execution for multimodal document RAG, and DocXEval benchmarks explainability in document understanding models.
editorial.why_it_matters: Document-QA agents are moving from one generalist tool-using model toward routed, role-specific stages, and explainability is now being measured separately from accuracy.
editorial.take_for_builders: Keep retrieval and reading as separate, individually evaluable stages in document-QA pipelines, and wait for released code or shared benchmarks before replacing a working setup with these preprints.

status.detail: Three arXiv preprints, no production releases: agent architecture for multimodal document RAG is converging on routing, while explainability evaluation lags.

beats.headline: Role-specialized tool agents split locating from reading
beats.summary: Separates retrieval tools from reading tools instead of giving one model both.

open_questions: Do RouteDRAG or the locate-judge-read agents publish code or benchmark numbers on a shared multimodal document QA set?
Does any production document-QA product adopt routed or role-specialized retrieval and reading stages?
Do later papers report DocXEval explainability scores for the agentic RAG systems in this thread?
